briefing.summary: Adds **email invitations to orgs**. An admin creates an invite, a background job emails a 7-day link, and the invitee accepts it to join the org with the invited role.

verdict.reason: This PR adds a **new way to gain membership in an org**. Rocky drafted 1 critical and 3 high findings, all on the auth path. The UI and wiring look routine.

reviewPath.why: New path that grants org membership and sets the member's role.
Public API surface that touches org permissions.
Schema migration that stores a credential (the invite token).
Handles personal data (email) and a credential (token).

checkedOk: Tenant RLS policy on the new table
Input validated with zod and the role enum restricted
Tokens are 256-bit and come from a CSPRNG
No new dependencies (lockfile has only a patch bump)

memoryApplied.text: Secrets and tokens are stored hashed
Never log emails, tokens or code

flags.text: Token uses 32 bytes from `crypto.randomBytes`. That's enough entropy.
Lookup by raw token. That only works because the token is stored in plaintext (see migration finding).
The invite's email is never compared with `user.email`, so anyone holding the link can join. That's fine for shareable links but not for invites meant for one person. Which is it?

noise.summary: One patch bump, `zod 4.6.5 → 4.6.6`. No new packages, and no install scripts changed.
Types regenerated from `openapi.yaml` for the two new endpoints. No hand edits found.

findings.title: Invitee can choose their own role, e.g. admin
findings.body: `requestedRole` comes straight from `req.body.role` and overrides the role the admin invited them with. Anyone with a member invite can send `{"role":"admin"}` and join as an admin.
findings.agentPrompt: In src/auth/invitations.ts, remove the requestedRole parameter from acceptInvitation and always use invite.role. Update the caller in src/api/routes/invitations.ts and add a test that a member invite cannot be accepted as admin.

findings.title: No permission check: any logged-in user can invite to any org
findings.body: `requireSession` only checks that the user is logged in. A user from org A can create invitations, including admin invites, for org B by changing `:orgId`.
findings.agentPrompt: Add requireOrgRole("admin") to POST /orgs/:orgId/invitations in src/api/routes/invitations.ts and add a test that a non-admin gets 403.

findings.title: Invitations can be reused after they're accepted
findings.body: `acceptedAt` gets set but is never checked, so one link can add any number of accounts until it expires.

lines: if (invite.expiresAt < new Date()) throw new Gone("invitation expired");
if (invite.acceptedAt) throw new Gone("invitation already used");

findings.agentPrompt: In acceptInvitation (src/auth/invitations.ts), reject invitations whose acceptedAt is set, and add a test for reusing an invite.

findings.title: Invite token stored in plaintext
findings.body: Anyone who can read this table, or a backup of it, can accept any pending invite. Store a SHA-256 hash and look up by the hash.

memory.text: Secrets and tokens are stored hashed, never raw

findings.agentPrompt: Store invitation tokens hashed: change the column to token_hash bytea UNIQUE, hash with SHA-256 in createInvitation, and look up by hash in acceptInvitation.

findings.title: Deleting an org won't remove its invitations
findings.body: Without `ON DELETE CASCADE`, deleting an org either fails or leaves invitee emails behind. That breaks the org-deletion guarantee in the GDPR erasure path.

lines: org_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
suggestion.context: id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

memory.text: Org deletion must cascade to all tenant data

findings.agentPrompt: Add ON DELETE CASCADE to invitations.org_id in the migration.

findings.title: Logs the invitee's email address
findings.body: This puts personal data in the logs, which the logging policy doesn't allow. Log IDs instead.

memory.text: Never log emails, tokens or source code

findings.agentPrompt: In src/jobs/sendInviteEmail.ts, replace the log line so it logs inviteId and orgId instead of the email.

findings.title: Token in the URL path ends up in access logs
findings.body: Path parameters get recorded by proxies and access logs. Send the token in the POST body instead: `POST /invitations/accept { token }`.
findings.agentPrompt: Move the invitation token from the URL path to the JSON body of the accept endpoint, and update InvitePage.tsx.

findings.title: Membership and acceptedAt aren't written atomically
findings.body: If the second write fails, the user is a member but the invite still looks open. Wrap both writes in `db.transaction()`.
findings.agentPrompt: Wrap addMembership and the invitations update in acceptInvitation in a single db.transaction().

findings.title: Expired invite leaves the button spinning
findings.body: The API returns 410 for expired invites, but there's no catch, so `busy` stays true and the user sees nothing.
findings.agentPrompt: Handle errors in InvitePage accept(): reset busy and show a message for 410 (expired) and 404.

findings.title: Missing tests for the two riskiest behaviours
findings.body: There are no tests for reusing an invite (F3) or overriding the role (F1). Both should fail today.
findings.agentPrompt: Add tests to src/auth/invitations.test.ts: reusing an accepted invite is rejected, and a member invite cannot be accepted as admin.
